did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jeremiah’s prophecy in this chapter was given at the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.
Did you know? The Lord commanded Jeremiah to stand in the temple courtyard and speak to all who came to worship, without omitting a single word of the message he had been commanded to deliver.
Did you know? The warning was not given merely to announce punishment, but to give the people an opportunity to hear, turn from their evil ways, and thereby prevent the disaster decreed against them.
Did you know? Jeremiah compared the future fate of the temple with that of Shiloh and warned that Jerusalem could become a curse to all the nations of the earth.

Did you know? After Jeremiah finished speaking, the priests, the prophets, and all the people seized him and demanded his death because they viewed his prophecy as a threat to the city and the temple.
Did you know? The priests and the prophets told the officials of Judah that Jeremiah’s prophecy against Jerusalem deserved the death penalty.
Did you know? Jeremiah did not withdraw his words, but he urged the people to reform their ways and deeds and obey the Lord, so that the disaster he had proclaimed would not come upon them.

Did you know? The elders of the land recalled Micah the Morashtite, who prophesied during the days of Hezekiah that Zion would be plowed like a field, Jerusalem would become ruins, and the Temple Mount would become like the high places of a forest.

Did you know? The elders cited Hezekiah’s response to Micah’s prophecy as a precedent: Hezekiah feared the Lord and pleaded with him, and the Lord relented concerning the disaster. Therefore, Jeremiah should not be put to death hastily.

Did you know? Ahikam son of Shaphan defended Jeremiah and prevented him from being handed over to the people to be put to death. In this way, Jeremiah escaped the fate of Uriah son of Shemaiah, who was executed during the reign of Jehoiakim.
